preview: Devanshi Shah shares her on-campus placement experience at Wells Fargo for an FTE role, detailing the online test, technical interview, managerial round, and final selection process.
content:
Devanshi Shah
CE BTech 2022 VJTI
Wells Fargo | FTE Interview | On-Campus
Wells Fargo had come at the start of the 2021 placement drive at VJTI in August. There were 4 rounds: online test, technical interview, managerial interview and HR round. Students from all branches were allowed to apply regardless of their CPI.

ROUND 1: ONLINE TEST (1 hr 40 mins)
Date: 8th August, 2021
It was at 11.00 am on AMCAT. There was a 30 min window to start the test.
There were 3 sections that had individual time limits and once a question was submitted, it could not be revisited.
1. Verbal Aptitude: It had questions like fill in the blanks, vocabulary and questions based on paragraphs. There were 15 mins to solve 14 questions. Moderate level English knowledge would suffice.
2. Business Logic: 15 questions to be solved in 25 mins. These were interpretation and analysis questions based on business graphs, tables, etc. They were doable if you think a little hard even if you’ve not practised them.
3. Coding: 2 questions (medium & hard) to be solved in 60 mins.
a. Bubble Burst
You are given an array with n integers indicating diameters of n consecutively placed bubbles. John can highlight bubbles from left to right whose diameter is greater than the neighbouring bubble to its left. After all the bubbles are highlighted, John could explode them. He then again starts from the first bubble. This process goes on until no more bubbles can be burst. You have to return the number of iterations for a given array.
Sample input: 3 6 9 8 2 10 6
Sample output: 2
Explanation:
Initial array: 3 6 9 8 2 10 6
After 1st iteration: 3 8 2 6
After 2nd iteration: 3 2
I did this by brute force and 16/17 test cases passed. In online tests, brute force solutions might work so try them out even if nothing else comes to your mind.
b. Maximum product path in a tree
An array with n integers was given containing values of n nodes of the tree. An mx2 matrix was given containing m edges. We had to return the maximum product of all nodes in a path from leaf to leaf. I was able to solve this partially.

All further rounds were scheduled for the next day 9 am onwards. 30 students were shortlisted for the next round.

ROUND 2: TECHNICAL INTERVIEW (50 mins)
Date: 9th August, 2021
The interview was held on Zoom. It started exactly at 10 am.
Surprisingly, I wasn’t asked to introduce myself. The interviewer had some mic issues so he called me instead and we were on Zoom muted.
He asked me to share my screen and open notepad. He asked me a LOT of questions but didn’t go deep into any of them.
DSA:
1. Which Data structures are you familiar with?
2. Sum of diagonal elements of an matrix
3. Types of linked lists
4. Difference between a stack and a queue

OOPs and C++/Java:
1. Pillars of OOP
2. Types of polymorphism
3. Pointers and References
4. Difference between abstract class and interface
5. Constructors and destructors, their types and syntax
6. Difference between class and struct, where are their objects stored (heap and stack respectively)

DBMS:
1. Indexing and its types
2. Explain Clustered indexing

Projects:
He had experience in Core Java, Spring Boot and Angular. I had worked on a project in Angular so I had a fair idea about it but not in depth about the underlying architecture and basics so I had communicated that beforehand when he started asking me questions about Angular.
1. How do applications on the internet communicate?
2. What are APIs? How do they work?
3. What are the different API methods?
4. Explain the use case of the POST method and how is it different from GET?
5. Basic questions about unit testing and deployment
6. How does Angular improve performance?
7. Folder structure of Angular and how does an Angular app run?
8. What are modules? What are directives?
And many more questions which I don’t remember now. He then asked me if I had any questions for him. He was in the same department at Wells Fargo as I was in my internship at Barclays so we discussed that and a little about my project there.

The moment the interview was over and I opened my phone, a message popped up saying my next interview was scheduled at 1.30 pm. 19 students were shortlisted for the next round.

ROUND 3: MANAGERIAL INTERVIEW (30 mins)
Date: 9th August, 2021
The course of this “interview” was very weird. The interviewer in this round was at a very senior position in the company and had 22 years of experience. He started by introducing himself followed by my introduction.
Then he asked me if I had any questions for him. I said I did and I could ask him or we could take them at the end. He said that it’s important for freshers to interact with senior managers and know the company and what it does. This was followed by the question, what do you know about Wells Fargo? I told him as much as I had heard in the PPT and I fumbled at places. Then he told me about the company and how technology is transforming banking.
What followed next was a database design question. For an online ecommerce system, where attributes can be added (schema can change) and there are a lot of reads, which database would you choose and why. I started with relational and then moved to non-relational because changing schemas could make things really complex in relational databases. This was more of a discussion but I couldn’t answer much.
He asked me briefly about my projects. Towards the end, again, he asked me if I had any questions for him and advised me to learn about database design and architecture.
This round was unusual because most others were asked about their resume and projects and in my case, the interviewer was speaking most of the time and the questions were completely different. I was considering this as a bad round.

11 students were called for the HR discussion. I didn’t get a call until late evening so I assumed that I was out of the process. I had interviews for one more company that day so everything added up to a lot of perturbation.
To my surprise, at about 8.15 pm, we received an email from them. They had chosen 7 people and I was one of them. They said that the offer was the result of the total score of the test and the interviews. Hence a few people, though the HR round did not happen for them, were selected. I then anticipated that the second round might’ve been a discussion and not an interview in my case.

LAST MINUTE ADVICE (kyuki prepare to kar hi liya hoga :))
1. Go through company archives to understand the pattern. Be prepared.
2. Research about the company (for managerial or HR rounds and to understand if you would actually like to work for them, benefits aside).
3. Ask GOOD questions at the end. Show your interest.
4. You will never be prepared enough and you can’t possibly know all the answers. It’s okay to goof up, let it go. Do what’s in your hand and leave the rest to destiny.
5. It’s good to be nervous. But don’t show it. Be confident. Don’t forget to smile :)

RESOURCES WHICH HELPED ME
1. Yash Jain ka Repo (This is GOLD)
2. Must Do Questions on GFG
3. 450 DSA by Love Babbar
4. Make a list of topics in each subject that you want to cover and watch videos or read about those topics. Don’t forget to cover examples and problems on those topics as well. Resources for this are vague (mostly YT and GFG)
